title: Affiliate Marketing for Small Businesses: How to Start Right

facts.fact: Research cited by the page shows that 97% of consumers look for reviews and recommendations before buying online (per PowerReviews, via BusinessWire).
facts.quote: Research shows that [97% of consumers](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20180319005257/en/PowerReviews-Finds-Virtually-Consumers-97-Percent-Depend) look for reviews and recommendations

facts.fact: The page states that affiliates are paid a commission only when an affiliate-driven sale occurs, and there is no upfront cost to recruit an affiliate.
facts.quote: you don’t pay anything to affiliates unless they generate a sale for you. You’re only paying when you see results – there’s no upfront cost to recruit an affiliate.

facts.fact: The page says the only real cost of affiliate marketing is the commissions paid to affiliates, and the brand sets the commission rates.
facts.quote: The only real cost is the commissions you give your affiliates. But since you set the commission rates, your risk is minimal

facts.fact: The page states that the guide covers 9 steps for starting an affiliate program.
facts.quote: 9 steps for starting a program without getting burned by affiliate networks.

facts.fact: The page states that affiliate marketing works best for ecommerce or digital product businesses, since physical products are generally easier for affiliates to promote on visual mediums like Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok.
facts.quote: Physical products are generally easier for affiliates to promote, particularly on more visual mediums like Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok.

facts.fact: The page advises small businesses to pay affiliate commissions only after a sale has been made, and not to pay per click or per lead.
facts.quote: it’s advisable to pay commissions only after a sale has been made. Don’t pay per click, and don’t pay per lead.

facts.fact: The page advises small businesses to research competitors' affiliate programs to estimate the average commission rate in their industry.
facts.quote: Research your competitor’s affiliate programs to get a sense of the average commission rate in your industry.

facts.fact: The page states that affiliate agreements should typically cover start and end dates, branding guidelines, promotional restrictions, commission rates and structure, and grounds for premature termination.
facts.quote: Affiliate agreements should typically cover: Definition of terms... Start and end dates of the agreement... Branding guidelines... Any marketing or promotional restrictions

facts.fact: The page advises small businesses to set affiliate program goals that can be achieved within a planned timeline, starting small and working up, and that goals can be based on affiliate traffic or branded search rather than only sales or revenue.
facts.quote: set a realistic goal for your affiliate program — one you can achieve within a planned timeline. Start with small goals and work your way up.

facts.fact: The page states that affiliate networks usually withhold affiliate data and limit a business's ability to build relationships with creators, so it advises against relying on a network to find affiliates.
facts.quote: Don’t rely on an affiliate network, as they usually withhold affiliaet data and limit your ability to build relationships with creators.

facts.fact: The page states that third-party affiliate networks hold on to a business's data and control all affiliate communication, unlike affiliate software.
facts.quote: which hold on to your data and control all affiliate communication.

facts.fact: The page says that at an early stage of business, micro-influencers with smaller but highly engaged followings are often more successful affiliate partners to connect with.
facts.quote: At this early stage, you’ll often find better success connecting with micro-influencers — new or niche content creators with smaller but tight-knit, highly engaged followings.

facts.fact: Affiliate networks are known to charge up to 30% commissions on sales, according to a third-party source cited by the vendor (amnavigator.com).
facts.quote: Affiliate networks are known to charge [up to 30% commissions]

facts.fact: Commission Junction (CJ Affiliate) network charges a $3,000 fee for initial setup, per the vendor's account.
facts.quote: the Commission Junction (CJ Affiliate) network charges a $3,000 fee for the initial setup.

facts.fact: The ShareASale network has a one-time $550 network access fee, per the vendor's account.
facts.quote: The ShareASale network has a one-time $550 network access fee, plus a $100 minimum deposit fee.
